function.name: introduction_greet
function.description: Generate a greeting message introducing a person and their relationship to another individual. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The name of the person being introduced.

relationship.description: The type of relationship to the related person.

related_person.description: The name of the person to whom the first person is related.

include_relationship.description: A flag to indicate whether to include the relationship in the greeting message.

message.content: I don’t have personal knowledge of specific individuals unless you share more context. If you’d like me to help introduce someone named Daniel (for example, as a friend, wife, etc.), just let me know the details and I can generate a greeting for you!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "do you know Daniel?" We need to respond appropriately. There's no mention of Daniel's identity. We can ask clarifying question or say we don't know. According to policy, we should not claim knowledge about private individuals. So we should respond that we don't have personal knowledge. We can ask if they want to introduce them. But we might also use the function to generate a greeting if they provide details. But the user hasn't provided details. So we should respond with a polite answer.
